question.text: Under the SEBI ODR framework on page 237 of the NISM Series-VII (January 2026) workbook, when an investor/client raises a complaint or dispute against a Market Participant, the conciliation fees are borne by:

answer.text: The MIIs, with the fees being recoverable from the Market Participant against whom the investor/client complaint is raised
The investor directly, at a SEBI-prescribed flat fee
The investor and the Market Participant in equal shares
SEBI, out of the Investor Protection Fund

explanation.text: The Logic: Page 237 of NISM Series-VII (January 2026) states that when an investor/client raises a complaint or dispute against a Market Participant, conciliation fees are borne by the MIIs and recovered from the Market Participant against whom the complaint is raised. The stem is now restricted to that investor/client-raised scenario, so this is the uniquely correct answer. The Trap: The investor never bears conciliation fees in the investor-raised scenario, and SEBI/IPF is not the funding source. The audit flagged the original because the same page 237 also says that when the Market Participant itself initiates the dispute, the Market Participant bears the conciliation fees directly - so without specifying who raised the dispute, the original key was over-broad. Note: The original was ambiguous because page 237 describes two scenarios (investor-raised vs Market-Participant-initiated) with different fee allocations, but the original stem did not distinguish them. The stem has been qualified to "investor/client raises a complaint or dispute against a Market Participant", which uniquely supports the MII-bears-and-recovers-from-MP answer.
